theme: फल-त्याग के साथ कर्म; contentment without dependence, freedom in action.
context: Krishna now makes the practical form of wisdom concrete. The wise person is not frozen by non-action, nor is the world rejected. Instead, action continues, but the doer does not cling to the result and does not build identity on success or failure.
contextHindi: अब कृष्ण wisdom का व्यावहारिक रूप स्पष्ट करते हैं। ज्ञानी व्यक्ति निष्क्रियता से नहीं जकड़ा रहता, न दुनिया से अलग हो जाता है। वह कर्म करता है, पर फल से चिपकता नहीं, सफलता-पराजय से अपना ‘मैं’ नहीं बनाता।
sanskritDevanagari:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः |
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ||४-२०||
transliteration:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ .
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto.api naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ ||4-20||

wordByWord.meaning: attachment to the fruit of action; clinging to the result.
ever content; rooted in inner sufficiency rather than external gain.
without support; not dependent on success, praise, or approval for inner stability.
though engaged in action; active in the world, but not possessed by it.
does nothing at all; in a karmic sense, he does not create bondage through action.

spokenHindi: श्रीकृष्ण कहते हैं कि मनुष्य फल से आसक्ति छोड़कर भी कर्म में लगा रह सकता है। ‘कर्मफलासङ्ग’ का अर्थ है कर्म के फल से लगाव। ‘नित्यतृप्त’ यानी सदा संतुष्ट, और ‘निराश्रय’ यानी किसी सहारे पर निर्भर न होना। श्लोक ऐसे व्यक्ति का वर्णन करता है जो काम में पूरी तरह लगा हुआ है, फिर भी ‘कुछ नहीं करता।’ इसका अर्थ यह नहीं कि वह निष्क्रिय है या केवल शरीर से जुड़े काम करता है। वह सोचता है, निर्णय लेता है और अपने काम पूरे करता है। बात यह है कि वह कर्म को अपने अहंकार और फल की आसक्ति से नहीं जोड़ता। इसलिए कर्म उसे बाँधता नहीं। यह श्लोक यह नहीं कहता कि वह पाप या मुक्ति का कारण नहीं बनता; यह कहता है कि फल की आसक्ति छोड़ने पर कर्म से बंधन नहीं होता। हमारे लिए अभ्यास यह है: काम ईमानदारी से करें, पर नतीजे को अपनी पहचान न बनाएँ।
clearEnglish: Krishna moves from character to daily practice. “Having abandoned attachment to the fruit of action” is not cynicism; it means the doer is not fused with outcome. The person is “ever content,” not complacent but inwardly stable. To be “without support” is to refuse to construct one’s worth on success, failure, approval, or rejection. The result is that even when engaged in action, the person does not accumulate karmic grip. This is not passivity, because the body continues to function, duties continue, and effort remains. What disappears is the hidden claim: “I did this; I must receive the result.” That claim creates bondage. A person who has relinquished that claim can still work, speak, decide, and serve, but without becoming a victim of outcome. In modern terms, this is the discipline of doing your job without making your identity depend on the result.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states that after giving up attachment to results, remaining content and free from dependence, one can still act without becoming bound by action.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The practical lesson is that whether we are working, waiting, or recovering, the real test is whether our inner peace depends on outcomes. Freedom grows when action remains sincere but not possessive.

practicalApplication.label: Work without ownership
practicalApplication.text: When you complete an assignment, do not immediately ask, “What did I get?” Instead ask, “Was I honest, careful, and aligned with my values?”

practicalApplication.label: Inner steadiness
practicalApplication.text: When criticism or praise arrives, pause and notice whether your self-worth changed. Return to your deeper standard instead of external approval.

reflectionQuestion: What would change in your work if you stopped treating success or failure as a verdict on your worth?
reflectionQuestionHindi: अगर आप सफलता या असफलता को अपने मूल्यों के निर्णय के रूप में नहीं मानें, तो आपके कार्य में क्या बदलाव आएगा?
